column1: # ZAP rules for .github/workflows/dast.yml (baseline + API scan). Format: <rule id>TAB<IGNORE|INFO|WARN|FAIL>TAB<note>.
# Lines starting with # are ignored by the ZAP scripts. Anything not listed keeps ZAP's default (WARN).
# Policy: an IGNORE needs a written justification that holds for PRODUCTION, not just for CI.
# OUTOFSCOPE takes a URL regex in the third column and silences the rule ONLY for matching URLs.
# Expected WARNs that we deliberately do NOT ignore (so a regression still shows up in the report):
#   10010 Cookie No HttpOnly Flag  - expected ONLY for vsh_csrf (double-submit token read by the SPA);
#                                    any other cookie in this alert is a bug (vsh_session must be HttpOnly).
#   90004 Insufficient Site Isolation (COEP/CORP) - not yet decided; tracked.
# First full run (Oct 2026, docs/release/production-readiness.md): 0 FAIL. Fixed then and escalated
# below so they cannot regress: 10036 (nginx version), 10055 (CSP 'unsafe-inline'), 90003 (SRI on
# third-party Google Fonts, now self-hosted). The same run led to the X-Forwarded-For trust fix
# (backend/tests/test_proxy_headers.py and the spoofing probe step in dast.yml). The API scan is fed real
# demo-tree IDs (dast-ids.prop): with placeholder path IDs 99% of its requests stopped at UUID validation.
# That ID-aware run found a NUL byte in a query string turning into an unhandled 500 (now a 422; see
# backend/tests/test_input_robustness.py).
# ---- scoped false positives (each limited to the URLs where the justification holds)
# (Private IP Disclosure) /auth/sessions lists the signed-in user's OWN sessions with their client IP, by design
# (so they can spot and revoke unknown sessions). In CI that IP is the Docker bridge (private); in production it is
# the user's own public address. Still reported anywhere else.
# (Unexpected Content-Type) The API scan also crawls the site root, where the SPA rightly serves HTML/JS/CSS.
# Every /api/ response must stay JSON, so the rule remains active for /api/ URLs.
# (Unexpected Content-Type) The family archive export is a download and is application/zip by design.
# ---- justified IGNOREs

column3: (Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set) CI scans plain HTTP on localhost. In production TLS terminates at the load balancer and the API sets HSTS whenever VSH_COOKIE_SECURE=true, which VSH_ENV=production enforces (config.validate_production).
(Cookie Without Secure Flag) Same reason: CI is plain HTTP so VSH_COOKIE_SECURE=false; production refuses to start without VSH_COOKIE_SECURE=true.
(Modern Web Application) Informational only: the frontend is a React SPA by design (ADR-0001), which just tells ZAP to use the AJAX spider.

(Storable and Cacheable Content / Non-Storable Content) Informational: hashed /assets/* are deliberately cacheable (immutable); HTML shell and every API response are deliberately Cache-Control: no-store.

column1: # ---- escalations: these fail the workflow

column3: (Server Leaks Version Information) nginx runs with server_tokens off.
(CSP misconfiguration, e.g. style-src 'unsafe-inline') the CSP is 'self'-only for scripts, styles and fonts.
(Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing) no third-party scripts or styles: fonts are self-hosted.
(Anti-clickjacking header missing) X-Frame-Options DENY / frame-ancestors 'none' must be on every response.
(X-Content-Type-Options missing) nosniff must be on every response.
(Content Security Policy header not set) CSP must be on every HTML and API response.
(Cross-Domain Misconfiguration) CORS must stay limited to VSH_CORS_ORIGINS with credentials.
